translations.text: The word of the Lord came to Jonah son of Amittai, and he said to him:
“Get up and go to Nineveh, the great city, and preach to them, because the outcry over their wickedness has risen to me.”

Jonah went away, fleeing to the land of Tarshish from the presence of the Lord. He went down to the city of Joppa and found a ship sailing to the land of Tarshish. He paid the ship’s fare and [?] boarded it to sail with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of the Lord.
The Lord brought a great wind upon the sea. The storm on the sea grew violent, and their ship was in danger of breaking apart.

The sailors were afraid, and they all cried out to their gods. They brought out and threw [?] into the sea to lighten their ship. But Jonah went down into the hold of the ship, fell asleep, and snored.
The captain went down to him and said, “Why are you sleeping? Get up and call on your God, so that God [?] may save us and we may not die.”
They said to one another, “Come, let us cast lots.” And the lot fell on Jonah.
They said to him, “Tell us on whose account this disaster has come upon us. What is your occupation? Where have you come from? Where are you going? Where is your country, and what is your people?”
He said to them, “I am a servant of the Lord, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
The men were terribly afraid and said to him, “What have you done?” The men knew that he had fled from the presence of the Lord, because he had told them.
They said to him, “What, then, shall we do to you so that the sea will leave us alone?” For the sea was growing turbulent, and great waves were rising.
Jonah said to them, “Pick me up and throw me into the sea, and the sea will leave you alone. I know that this great storm has come upon you because of me.”
The men struggled to return to land, but they could not, because the sea was growing turbulent and rising against them.

They all cried out together to the Lord and said, “Far be it from you, Lord! Do not destroy us on account of this man’s life. Do not hold us guilty of [?] an innocent man, for you, Lord, have done as you wished.”
They picked up Jonah [?] and threw him into the sea, and the sea became calm.
Those men feared the Lord greatly. They offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made vows.
The Lord commanded a great whale to swallow Jonah, and Jonah remained in the whale’s belly for three days and three nights.
Jonah prayed to the Lord his God from inside the belly of the great sea creature.
He said, “In my distress I cried out to the Lord my God, and he heard me. From the belly of Sheol came my cry, and he heard my voice.
“You threw me into the heart of the deep sea, and rivers surrounded me. All your waves and surges came and passed over me.
“But I said, ‘Have you then cast me away from before your eyes? Will I see your holy temple again?’
Water poured in, threatening my life. The deep trapped me below, and my head was submerged.
“Into the clefts of the mountains I went down [?], into the earth whose bars have been shut since the creation of the world. Let my life rise to you without destruction, Lord my God.
“When my life was fading, I remembered the Lord. Let my prayer reach you in your holy temple.
“Those who cling to emptiness and falsehood abandon their mercy.
“But I will sacrifice to you with words of praise and thanksgiving. What I vowed for my life I will pay to the Lord.”
The Lord commanded that whale, and it brought Jonah out onto the land.
The word of the Lord came [?] to Jonah [?], and he said to him:
“Get up and go to Nineveh, the great city, and preach to them according to the first proclamation that I told you.”
Jonah [?] got up and went to Nineveh, as the Lord had told him. Nineveh was an exceedingly great city in God’s sight, a journey of three days on foot.
He began [?] to enter the city and preached after a day’s journey, saying, “In three days Nineveh will be overthrown.”
The people of Nineveh believed the word of God. They proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, both small and great.
The king of Nineveh heard, rose from his throne, took off his robes, put on sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
The king proclaimed to Nineveh, to its small and great, saying, “People and animals, cattle and sheep, must not eat anything or graze, [?] water.”
People and animals put on sackcloth and cried out to God together. They abandoned all their evil conduct and the violence in their hands, and said:
“Who knows whether God will relent and turn away the scourge of his wrath, so that we will not die?”
God saw their deeds, that they had turned away from their evil [?]. God also relented concerning the harm he had said he would bring upon them, and he did not bring that harm.
Jonah was deeply distressed and grieved.

He prayed to God and said, “Lord, is this not what I said in my own country? This is why I fled to Tarshish, because I know that you are merciful and compassionate, slow to anger and abundant in mercy, and that you relent concerning harm.
“And now, Lord, take my life from me, because it is better for me to die than to live.”
God said to Jonah, “Are you so deeply distressed?”
Then Jonah went out of the city and sat at the city gate. He made himself a shelter and sat beneath its shade until he could see what would happen to the city.
God commanded a gourd plant, and it grew and shaded Jonah’s head, to shelter him from his suffering. Jonah was very glad because of the gourd plant.
On the following day God commanded a worm, and it killed this gourd plant, and it withered.
When the sun rose, God commanded a scorching hot wind, and the sun beat painfully on Jonah’s head. He grew faint and was angry about his life. He said, “It is better for me to die than to live.”
God said to Jonah, “Are you so deeply distressed because of the gourd plant?” He said, “I am deeply distressed, even to the point of death.”
God said to him, “You pity a gourd plant for which you did not labor and which you did not water, which grew in a night and died in a night.”
“And should I not have compassion on Nineveh, the great city, where there are more than one hundred and twenty thousand people who do not know their left hand from their right, and many animals?”
